newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoran secessionists protest, reject delegation.
newsitem.headline: Comoran secessionists protest, reject delegation.

text.p: Demonstrators on the Indian Ocean island of Moheli took to the streets for a second consecutive day on Wednesday and Comoran secessionists rejected a delegation sent by the government.
Witnesses said protesters who want Moheli to leave the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros built barricades and raised French flags in Moheli's capital Fomboni as they did on Wednesday.

Pro-secessionists on Moheli, the smallest island in the Comoros archipelago with 25,000 people, called for a general strike on Monday to push for independence and support residents of Comoros' second island Anjouan who also want to secede.
"We will show the Comoran authorities on Monday that we are fed up of being permanently humiliated," a Moheli secessionist leader told Reuters.
The Comoro Islands, which has some 670,000 people, became independent from France in 1975.
But many residents of Anjouan and Moheli say independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and coups, and want to return to French rule or break away from the Islamic republic.
Secessionists on Anjouan said on Tuesday they had elected their 75-year-old leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim as "president" of their breakaway state.

Ibrahim's government held its second meeting on Thursday and decided to reject a delegation of native Anjouans living on the main island of Grand Comoros, sent by the Comoran government in a bid to persuade the Anjouan secessionists to reconsider.
"I don't delude myself, our mission is doomed to failure since the Anjouan people are obviously deeply committed to separation," one of the delegation said.
The Anjouan secessionists plan a rally during next weekend's visit by Organisation of African Unity (OAU) envoy Pierre Yere of Ivory Coast, who was charged on Wednesday with meeting both sides.
Anjouan's poverty contrasts with the relative prosperity of the island of Mayotte, which voted to remain French in 1975.
France has denounced the secessionists, saying the Anjouan situation is serious and could destabilise the whole region.
Comoran President Mohamed Taki said last week the islands would be given more autonomy and would be divided into communes.
